title: 搜索需求出现后，怎样建议先试一个新品？
topic: 结合搜索需求和现有产能提出小范围产品测试

source.title: Follow the grain: How a woodworking business grew 300% by tracking trends
source.section: Follow the grain: How a woodworking business grew 300% by tracking trends
source.type: Amazon 官方卖家业务增长案例
source.context: Amazon 官方业务材料；本课练习围绕实际业务沟通任务。
paragraphs: “Our wood signs, the bread and butter of our business, was on its last leg. We knew we needed to evolve,” said Tim. Using Amazon’s data-driven tools, like Product Opportunity Explorer to identify what products customers were searching for, he decided to pivot the business from wooden signs to customized shelving.
“We were looking for a product that we could make utilizing the same equipment we already used,” recalled Tim. “From poring over the Amazon data, we realized there was a need for shelving.”

It was a strategy that paid off. Since launching the shelving line in April, sales have climbed 58% year over year. Unlike seasonal farmhouse signs, shelving solves an everyday problem—covering wire closet racks and upgrading pantry storage—making it less vulnerable to shifting décor trends.
translations: “木制招牌是我们业务的支柱产品，但已经快做不下去了。我们知道必须转型。”Tim 说。他利用亚马逊的数据工具（如 Product Opportunity Explorer）了解顾客正在搜索哪些产品，决定从木制招牌转向定制收纳架。
Tim 回忆说：“我们在找一种能用现有设备生产的产品。仔细研究亚马逊数据后，我们发现市场需要收纳架。”
这个策略奏效了。收纳架产品线于 4 月推出后，销售额同比增长了 58%。与受季节性家居装饰趋势影响的农舍风格招牌不同，收纳架解决的是日常问题——遮住铁丝衣橱架、改善食品储物空间，因此不容易受到家居装饰潮流变化的影响。
fullTextParagraphs: When Tim Schafer was laid off in 2017, he and his wife, Paige, saw it as a blessing. The couple ran Schafer Art Studio, a home décor business specializing in farmhouse-style wooden signs, selling mostly through their Amazon Handmade storefront. Since 2015, Tim would return from his nine-to-five and spend his nights and weekends in his woodworking studio.
“By the time I was laid off, I was exhausted,” Tim recalled. “I went through the seven stages of grief on my drive home, and then I was ready for the next chapter of my life.”

Paige was happy too, realizing the change could be a catalyst for their business, allowing them the time and focus to invest in expanding their inventory. Their first thought was to enroll in Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA), allowing them to send inventory into Amazon’s fulfillment network and outsource packing, shipping, customer service and returns, ensuring they could keep products in stock and meet growing demand.
“With Fulfillment by Amazon, we can get a bunch of product ready and send it in, and then sell it while we’re sleeping,” said Paige. “We’re making sales without having to get up and pack an item.”
Paige and Tim Schafer started selling handmade wooden signs in 2017 and have grown their business by 300% leveraging Amazon data for product expansion.
Today, FBA accounts for 20% of their revenue. Their remaining business is custom work, which the Schafers deliver using Fulfillment by Merchant (FBM).

“Using FBA and FBM together has been integral for our business,” said Paige. “It means we can continue to do customized work, letting the customer pick the size, stain and wording of the signs, while also having a sales stream that’s more automatic.”

In addition to simplifying fulfillment, Amazon made it easier for the Schafers to access the legal protections necessary in running a business, including trademark support and liability insurance. Using Amazon’s IP Accelerator program, they were able to choose a lawyer from Amazon’s network of vetted professionals to copyright their brand quickly.

“It normally takes six months or a year to get your copyright or trademark set up. But because I went through IP Accelerator, I was granted all the benefits of being a brand-registered business right away,” said Paige.

Amazon’s support had an immediate impact on their business. Within a year, sales increased 300%. The biggest value of Amazon, though, has been the tools that help them tweak their strategy when sales slow.
The company now offers more than 100 products, blending batch-produced items fulfilled through Amazon.

“Our wood signs, the bread and butter of our business, was on its last leg. We knew we needed to evolve,” said Tim. Using Amazon’s data-driven tools, like Product Opportunity Explorer to identify what products customers were searching for, he decided to pivot the business from wooden signs to customized shelving.
“We were looking for a product that we could make utilizing the same equipment we already used,” recalled Tim. “From poring over the Amazon data, we realized there was a need for shelving.”

It was a strategy that paid off. Since launching the shelving line in April, sales have climbed 58% year over year. Unlike seasonal farmhouse signs, shelving solves an everyday problem—covering wire closet racks and upgrading pantry storage—making it less vulnerable to shifting décor trends.
“It’s something people need, not just something they want,” said Tim. “And because we’re looking at the data in Product Opportunity Explorer, we can see when a product has staying power.”

The couple now offers more than 100 products in their Amazon store, blending batch-produced items fulfilled through FBA with highly customized pieces shipped directly from their home workshop. In a workshop based in their home—converted from their living room and garage—plywood is cut, stained and finished by hand before heading out to customers nationwide.

With so many different products, the Schafers have found particular value in A+ Content, which has enabled them to enhance listings and their product pages with high-quality photos and videos showing how each product is made and customized.
“Being able to show customers that this is handmade in Oregon by real people makes a difference,” said Paige. “A+ Content gave us space to tell that story.”
Paige, a former fourth-grade teacher, has mentored other artisans in the area, helping several launch their own Amazon Handmade stores.
For Tim, the shift from corporate America to local manufacturing has reshaped how he defines success.
“In corporate, you can do everything right and still be expendable,” he said. “Here, if we bring a great product to life and customers love it, we see that directly. The feedback is immediate.”

That direct connection extends beyond their customers. The couple sources wood locally whenever possible, keeping production rooted in Oregon. Paige, a former fourth-grade teacher, has also mentored other artisans in the area, helping several launch their own Amazon Handmade stores and navigate fulfillment options.
“I love showing people they can do this too,” she said. “You don’t need a warehouse. You can start small, learn the tools, and grow.”
Looking ahead, the Schafers plan to expand their shelving line with coordinating storage accessories, using Amazon’s data to guide what customers want next.
“Trends come and go,” said Tim. “You just have to keep evolving.The audience is there. If you’re willing to learn and adapt, you can keep building.”

scenario.title: 模拟情境：根据需求信号提出新品试点
english: Sales of your team's seasonal wall signs are slowing down.
Search data shows steady interest in custom closet shelving, which can be made with existing equipment.
Recommend a small product test, explain the evidence, and set a measure for deciding whether to expand.
chinese: 团队的季节性木制招牌销量正在放缓。
搜索数据显示，顾客持续关注定制衣橱收纳架，而且现有设备就能生产。
请建议先做小范围产品测试，说明依据，并提出决定是否扩大的衡量指标。

firstAttempt.prompt: 木制招牌销量放缓，搜索数据显示顾客持续关注定制收纳架，而且现有设备可以生产。请建议如何小范围测试，并说明依据和决定是否扩大的指标。
firstAttempt.sample: Sales of our seasonal wall signs are slowing down, but search data shows steady interest in custom closet shelving that we can make with our existing equipment. I recommend testing a small batch before expanding. We should track sell-through and customer feedback during the test.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先把需求信号和可用产能连起来，再提出小规模测试，最后说明用什么结果决定是否扩大。

structure.original: Using Amazon’s data-driven tools, like Product Opportunity Explorer to identify what products customers were searching for, he decided to pivot the business from wooden signs to customized shelving.
analysis: 句首 Using… 说明作出决定时参考了什么工具和信息。
to identify… 说明使用工具的目的。
decided to pivot from A to B 表示把业务方向从 A 转向 B。
structure.transfer: Using search data to identify what customers need, we can test a small batch before committing to a wider launch.

rewrite.bad: The old product was not popular, so the team tried something else.
rewrite.good: Sales of the seasonal wall signs are slowing down, but search data shows steady interest in customized shelving. We can make it with our existing equipment, so I recommend testing a small batch before expanding. We should track sell-through and customer feedback during the test.
rewrite.translation: 季节性木制招牌的销量正在放缓，但搜索数据显示顾客持续关注定制收纳架。现有设备就能生产，所以我建议扩大之前先做小批量测试，并在测试期间关注售出率和顾客反馈。
rewrite.pattern: Sales of [current product] are slowing down, but search data shows interest in [new product]. We can use [existing resource] to test a small batch and track [measure] before expanding.

cloze.why: sales are slowing down 表示销量正在放缓。

cloze.prompt: Search data shows steady ______ in custom shelving.
cloze.why: interest in + 产品表示对某种产品有持续兴趣。

cloze.prompt: We should test a small batch ______ expanding.
cloze.why: before expanding 表示扩大之前先测试。

choice.prompt: 搜索数据显示顾客关注定制收纳架，而且现有设备可以生产。哪条建议最稳妥？
options: Search data shows interest, so we should launch every variation immediately.
We can use the existing equipment to test a small batch, track sell-through and customer feedback, and expand if the results support it.
The old product is slowing down, so there is no need to check customer demand.
choice.why: 先用现有产能做小范围测试，再根据售出情况和顾客反馈决定是否扩大。

output.prompt: 团队的节日礼盒销量下滑，客户搜索显示日常收纳需求上升，而且现有包装线可以改造使用。请用英文提出新品试水方案，并说明要看哪些数据。
output.sample: Our holiday gift boxes are losing momentum, while search data points to steady demand for everyday storage. We can adapt the existing packaging line, so I recommend testing two storage products first. We should track conversion, repeat purchases, and margin before deciding whether to expand.
check: 说出旧产品遇到的问题和新需求证据
说明可复用的现有资源
给出小规模测试和复盘指标

blockers: 人工听审音频，逐条确认与页面文字一致并检查语速、停顿和截断。
真实账号进度保存和生产环境逐期验收。
